_what: Live sweep of previously-unrendered spread (base, operand) pairs. Headers confirmed rendered by preview_strategy_report; every one matched omega.fanout.outputs_for exactly.

batches._recording: Headers generated from the rendered plan rather than re-keyed from the response. Safe only because every header in the response matched outputs_for exactly - verified against the returned conditionColumns before recording.

_complete.arithmetic: 1,712 spread pairs were untested when the sweep began. 357 of them turned out to be illegal - the series-chain operand rule, found by this sweep at pair 545 - and were removed from the space rather than excused from the count. 1712 - 357 = 1355, which is exactly what was rendered.
_complete.verification: Every batch was checked by scripts/record_spread_batch.py as an EXACT ORDERED comparison against omega.fanout.outputs_for, and the recorder refuses to write anything unless the returned headers equal the predicted headers in the same order, and refuses to record a batch number twice. 0 mismatches across all 11.
_complete.whatThisProves: Every shape omega can emit renders on the live platform, and omega predicts its headers exactly. The gap between 'omega says legal' and 'the platform accepts it' is closed for the column layer as of this date.
_complete.whatThisDoesNotProve: That the shapes STAY legal - the contract goes stale after deployments, which is why 12 platform defects are on record. Nor does it say anything about whether any column is USEFUL, or whether its VALUE is correct - this is a legality and header-prediction result and nothing more. Value correctness is a separate question, answered separately in docs/19.
_complete.costAndCaps: 11 renders. THREE separate caps bind at different times and all three were measured rather than assumed: estimatedTokens 16,000 binds on wide unchained batches at ~32 tokens/header; the same budget on chained batches costs ~46/header because their preamble text is longer; and mcp_result_bytes 256,000 binds FIRST on trajectory batches at ~586 bytes/header - a 480-header batch returned 281,346 bytes and was refused while estimatedTokens sat at ~13k of 16k.
